description.value: This study investigated associations between chronotype and amygdala BOLD response and amygdala-fronto-limbic functional connectivity during an implicit emotion processing task in healthy participants.

spans.text: Here, fifty healthy, right-handed individuals without a current or previous diagnosis of depression, family history of depression or sleep disorder underwent functional magnetic resonance imaging (FMRI).

description.value: Observational cross-sectional study of healthy participants.

Chronotype was determined using the 5-item reduced Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire ( ), based on the full version of the MEQ validated for a young adult population (18-32 years).

description.value: The 5-item reduced Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire was administered to determine individual chronotype. Scores ranged from 6 to 20 in the sample (mean 12.62, SD 3.62); higher scores indicated earlier chronotype and lower scores later chronotype.

spans.text: Chronotype was determined using the 5-item reduced Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire
Sleep quality was assayed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index ( ).

description.value: The Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index was administered to assess sleep quality. Scores ranged from 1 to 15 in the sample (mean 7.30, SD 3.42; original scale 0–21), and PSQI score was also used as a covariate.

spans.text: Sleep quality was assayed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index

description.value: The Patient Health Questionnaire-4 measured mood and anxiety symptoms. Anxiety scores ranged from 0 to 5 (mean 0.91, SD 1.09) and mood scores from 0 to 6 (mean 1.61, SD 1.58); mood and anxiety were also summed for covariate adjustment.

Functional MR data were acquired using a T2*-weighted echo planar imaging sequence (EPI, TR = 2000 ms, TE = 31 ms, FA = 85°, FOV = 192 × 192 × 87 mm 3 [29 slices, voxel size = 3 × 3 × 3 mm 3 ], number of measurements = 170, imaging bandwidth = 752 Hz/px, GRAPPA acceleration factor = 2).
